subject: Post-call recap + serving playbook for Dedicated capacity (Finova)
messages:

Subject: Post-call recap + serving playbook for Dedicated capacity (Finova)

Thanks again for the call earlier, Alex — good to meet the Finova team. This thread is a concise recap + proposed next steps so we can size Dedicated and unblock your architecture review. I flagged a few follow-ups for our infra and product folks.

Recap (what you told us)
- Peak peak: ~120 req/s during trading-batch windows (primarily inference for risk scoring).
- Typical request: ~400 tokens (prompt + context) for generation; embeddings batch jobs for nightly indexing.
- Latency SLO: P95 < 250ms for live scoring; background jobs can be higher.
- Security: SOC 2 expected; SSO/SCIM + SAML; prefer mTLS for Private/VPC.

Key technical asks you had
- Example Dedicated capacity config (autoscale, concurrency, queueing).
- Guidance on SDK integration (Java + Python), auth flow, and routing strategies for live vs. background.
- Recommended embedding / reranker pattern for semantic search so we keep latency under target while preserving quality.

Initial recommendations (high level)
1) Dedicated sizing: start with a conservative baseline of 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs for production, with burst pool reserved for 2x during peak windows. This provides headroom for model variants and faster KV cache warmup.
2) Concurrency & queues: set per-replica concurrency limits (e.g., 8 concurrent requests per GPU) and a request queue depth of 256 to smooth short bursts. Use a per-tenant request queue and a global admission limiter so background jobs can't starve live traffic.
3) Autoscale policy: scale on rolling 1-minute CPU + GPU utilization + request queue depth; prefer scheduled scaling for known trading windows.
4) Routing & SDK: use Redwood SDK for token streaming and structured output/tool-calling. Route live scoring to low-latency model variant (quantized when possible), and route heavy rerank/embedding workflows to dedicated background workers.
5) Embeddings + rerank: index using nightly batch embeddings (vector DB of choice). For query-time ranking: retrieve top-100 with ANN, then use a lightweight cross-encoder reranker (on Dedicated) to re-score top-K (K=10) to meet quality/latency tradeoffs.

Attachments: I attached a draft mutual action plan and a sizing workbook to play with numbers.

Next steps (proposed)
- You: confirm peak window schedule and whether 120 req/s is sustained or bursty by EOD Tue.
- Redwood: Sean to share a starter Dedicated config + example SDK auth snippet (mTLS + API key fallbacks).
- Joint: schedule a 30-min architecture walkthrough next week (prefer Wed 10am PT).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with detailed artifacts from Sean in this thread.

Best,

- 120 req/s is a sustained average during market open hours (9:30–11:30 ET), with short peaks up to ~200 req/s for 1–2 minute bursts.
- Typical response lengths are 60–120 tokens returned; we care most about P95 for live requests.
- Our infra team prefers mTLS for Private; we can do API keys for hosted but need SAML SSO for UI access.
- For embeddings: nightly bulk indexing (we can push batches of 64–256). We want the reranker to execute in <120ms on top-K when called.

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + serving playbook for Dedicated capacity (Finova)

Alex — thanks for the clarifications. Below are concrete starter configs and an architecture note. I kept the configuration conservative; we can iterate after telemetry from a pilot.

1) Starter Dedicated config (pseudoconfig for discussion)
--- begin config ---
cluster: finova-prod-dedicated
gpu_pool: a100-equivalent
replicas: 4
per_replica_concurrency: 8   # parallel in-flight requests per replica
request_queue_depth: 256    # per-tenant queue depth
burst_capacity: 2            # additional replicas that can be spun for short bursts
autoscale:
  min_replicas: 4
  max_replicas: 12
  metrics:
    - type: gpu_utilization
      window: 60s
      threshold: 70
    - type: request_queue_depth
      window: 30s
      threshold: 180
slo_targets:
  live_p95_latency_ms: 250
  reranker_p95_ms: 120
--- end config ---

Notes:
- Concurrency math: if one GPU can service ~8 concurrent requests at our expected token sizes, 4 replicas gives ~32 effective concurrency. For your 120 req/s sustained, that maps to ~3.75 req/s per concurrent slot — plenty with caching. If we see higher service time, autoscale will add replicas.
- Queueing: use backpressure + 429s for non-urgent background jobs; prioritize live scoring via token-level priority.

2) SDK / Auth patterns
- Python/Java SDK: use Redwood client with built-in retry/streaming. Example auth flows:
  * Hosted: API key (rotate regularly via Vault).
  * Dedicated/Private: mTLS to the node endpoint + short-lived exchange tokens for SDK (SDK does certificate pinning).
  * Admin console: SAML SSO + SCIM for group provisioning.

3) Routing & variants
- Use request metadata to route: {route: live, region: us-east, model_variant: lowlatency}. That lets you route live scoring to low-latency quantized variant while sending long-form generation or safety checks to higher-quality model variant.

4) Embeddings + rerank pattern
- Nightly embedding job: batch size 128, parallel workers, write to vector DB.
- Query path: ANN -> top-100 -> cross-encoder rerank on Dedicated for top-10. For latency: aim to run cross-encoder on cheap variant with model distillation to meet 120ms P95; if not possible, lower K and increase ANN recall.

5) Observability hooks
- Per-request token breakdown (SDK), model variant tag, latency and cache-hit metric. We’ll provide dashboards and a tracing hook you can forward to Datadog.

I attached a tiny diagram and the sizing workbook. If you want we can run a short load test with a dev cluster prior to committing to a capacity profile.

--
